prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2019 – Stop Brexit, Build a Brighter Future

Purpose and values: build and safeguard a fair, free and open society where liberty, equality and community thrive; disperse power, champion dignity, diversity and creativity; put people’s wellbeing and the planet first.

Stop Brexit to unlock a brighter, more generous, internationalist future:
- Revoke Article 50 with a Lib Dem majority; otherwise back a People’s Vote with the option to remain.
- Protect freedom of movement, scientific collaboration and peace in Northern Ireland; secure a £50bn “Remain Bonus” to invest in schools and tackling inequality.
- Extend civic rights to long‑term EU residents.

A stronger, fairer, innovation‑led green economy:
- £130bn infrastructure boost; £50bn Regional Rebalancing; a Green Investment Bank; wellbeing budgets, not GDP alone, guiding spending.
- Raise R&D to 3% of GDP; spread innovation beyond the South East; support creative industries and ethical tech.
- Back SMEs and entrepreneurs: hyper‑fast broadband, prompt‑payment enforcement, start‑up allowance, local banking.
- Fair taxes: restore Corporation Tax to 20%; tougher action on avoidance by tech giants; replace Business Rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy; tax income from wealth more like income from work.
- Modern work: a genuine Living Wage; new “dependent contractor” status with basic rights; flexible work from day one; higher minimum wage for zero‑hours at peak times; stronger worker voice (board representation, pay votes) and responsible corporate purpose.

World‑class education and skills:
- Free, high‑quality childcare from 9 months (35 hours, 48 weeks), tripled Early Years Pupil Premium, £1bn for Children’s Centres.
- Reverse school cuts; 20,000 extra teachers; clear the repairs backlog; SEND funding boost.
- End “teaching to the test”: scrap mandatory SATs, replace league tables, reform Ofsted.
- A “curriculum for life” and protection for arts.
- Lifelong learning: £10,000 Skills Wallet for every adult; stronger FE, maintenance grants restored; mental health standards in universities.

Climate action now and nature restored:
- Net zero by 2045; at least 80% renewable electricity by 2030; ban fracking; £6bn/yr to insulate homes and end fuel poverty by 2025.
- Clean Air Act; only new electric cars/vans by 2030; rail network ultra‑low‑emission by 2035; more buses, trams, walking and cycling.
- Nature Act; 60m trees a year; peatland and wetland restoration; Zero‑Waste & Resource Efficiency Act with plastics bans and right‑to‑repair.

Health and social care with parity for mental health:
- 1p on Income Tax raising £7bn/yr for the NHS and social care; £10bn capital; integrate services and end forced tendering.
- Mental health waiting‑time standards, 24/7 crisis care, maternal and perinatal support, community provision close to home.
- Workforce plan to end GP shortages; fair support for carers; evidence‑led public health (Wellbeing Strategy, obesity measures, PrEP, minimum unit pricing).
- Reform drug policy: a legal, regulated cannabis market focused on harm reduction.

A fair society: security, homes and safe communities:
- Fix Universal Credit: five‑day first payment; scrap two‑child limit and benefits cap; fair Local Housing Allowance; end punitive sanctions; legal right to food.
- Triple‑lock pensions; compensation for WASPI women.
- Build 300,000 homes a year including 100,000 social; zero‑carbon standards; renters’ security and “Help to Rent”; end rough sleeping in five years.
- Rural and coastal renewal: buses, broadband, local service hubs.
- Public‑health approach to crime: restore community policing; invest in youth services; presumption against short prison sentences; focus on rehabilitation and reducing reoffending.

Freedom, rights, equality and a humane migration system:
- Defend the Human Rights Act and ECHR; end bulk surveillance and police facial recognition; modernise family law.
- Tackle hate crime; reform the Gender Recognition Act; X passports; BSL Act; end period poverty; drive diversity and pay‑gap transparency.
- Scrap the hostile environment; 28‑day limit on detention; flexible work and student visas; right to work after 3 months for asylum seekers; expand refugee resettlement and family reunion.

Better politics and a federal UK:
- Proportional representation (STV); votes at 16; votes for long‑term EU residents and UK citizens abroad; reform the Lords; citizens’ assemblies; clean up party funding and online ads.
- Radical devolution of power and revenue; a written constitution for a federal United Kingdom.

A better world:
- Lead through the EU, UN, NATO and WTO; spend 0.7% on aid with climate and gender equality at the core; Magnitsky‑style sanctions.
- Suspend arms sales to Saudi Arabia; robust cyber defence; maintain a minimum nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament.
- Champion global climate action, biodiversity protection and an end to fossil fuel subsidies worldwide.
